retinoic acid promotes TGF-beta-induced Foxp3( ) expression in naive CD4( ) T cells indirectly, via negative regulation of a population of CD44(hi) CD4( ) effector T cells.

In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of action of RA and the effects of RA on Foxp3+ cell development and function.
the mechanisms by which TGF-beta promotes the generation of Foxp-3(+) regulatory T cells and the role of RA in this process.
understanding the molecular and cellular mechanisms by which RA and TGF-β regulate the development and function of Foxp3( )Tregs, and the role of Foxp3 ( ) Tregs in regulating immune responses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RA enhances Foxp3 expression in naive CD4+ T cells by a mechanism that involves the negative regulation by CD4+ CD4hi T cells of TGF-β-mediated Foxp3 expression.
RA can directly promote Treg cell conversion in naive CD4+ T cells, although it is not clear whether RA can promote Foxp3 expression in the absence of TGF-beta.
RA can promote TGF-β-mediated Foxp3+ Treg conversion of naive T cell in vitro by inhibiting the suppressive activity of CD4+CD25-CD44hi Treg cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RA can directly or indirectly promote TGF-β-mediated conversion of naive T cell into Foxp3+ Treg cells.
retinoic acid promotes Foxp3 induction in naive T cells in the presence of TGF-beta by acting on the surrounding environment.

RA does not directly act on the naive T cells to induce Foxp3 expression, but rather indirectly by removing a negative influence on Foxp3 expression from an accompanying population of CD4+ CD4hi effector/memory cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RA can directly promote Foxp3 expression by naive T cells.
RA can directly promote Foxp3 expression in the absence of CD4+CD25+ Tregs.
RA does not directly promote Foxp3 expression in naive T cells.
